messages:
ginny: quick check — running a semantic-fingerprint stability pass on the new fn-embed-v2-int4. small additive noise (sigma=0.01) on inputs seems to shift cluster centroids more than i'd expect. recall@10 drops ~2.4% on our dev holdout. :thinking:

samir: can you paste the eval command you ran? also which tokenizer / preprocess pipeline?

ginny: ran from the eval harness: `python ci/eval_fingerprint.py --model fn-embed-v2 --quant int4 --noise 0.01 --holdout datasets/dev-anchors.jsonl --seed 42 --topk 10`

leo: interesting — did you use per-channel quant or symmetric? int4 per-tensor has been flaky on that model in my last run.

ginny: per-channel, we tested both. per-channel int4 slightly better but still noisy. baseline (fp16) recall@10 = 0.873, int4 = 0.851 at noise=0.01.

tara: can you dump the top-1 id flip list for a few examples? might be dataset edgecases rather than global shift.

ginny: here, short sample:
```
query_id: Q_12431
fp16_top1: DOC_993
int4_top1: DOC_2895
cos(fp16,int4): 0.62
```

samir: low cos is concerning. run the gaussian jitter sweep (0, 1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2) and compute the distribution of cosine sim between fp16 fingerprint and quant fingerprint per-query. also compute topk id-flip rate.

leo: add a check for prefix-KV caching artifact — if we ran warm-starts with different batch sizes it can alter runtime ordering and produce nondet quant rounding in some kernels. include `--batch-seed` fixed.

tara: ran the sweep quick locally, results (recall@10):
- noise=0 => int4 0.857 vs fp16 0.874
- noise=1e-4 => int4 0.855
- noise=1e-3 => int4 0.849
- noise=1e-2 => int4 0.833
so int4 degrades faster with noise than fp16, seems like reduced margin.

eval-bot: CI run finished for fn-embed-v2-int4 on dev-anchors (run 3625300000): overall recall@10 delta = -0.022 vs baseline, top1 flip rate = 4.6%, mean cos sim = 0.78. See /ci/artifacts/3625300000/summary.html :eyes:

samir: mean cos=0.78 ok but that top1 flip 4.6% is high. can we isolate by cluster? compute per-cluster recall drop — maybe long-tail clusters are affected.

ginny: doing cluster stratification now — will bucket by cluster size and avg intra-cluster sim. initial glance: small clusters (n<50) have 3x flip rate vs big clusters.

leo: that points to reduced representational margin for sparse neighborhoods. try temp-scaling (multiply embeddings by 1.02) as a quick sanity to see if cosine thresholds move. also test L2 normalization robustness (we usually normalize, right?).

tara: we normalize before index. used `normalize=True` in indexer. temp-scaling didn't help much (tiny uptick).

ginny: next steps: 1) run per-channel vs per-tensor int4 sweep with batch-seed locked 2) run 10k-query fingerprint jitter with per-cluster stratification 3) run PQ fallback test (index-level) to see retrieval-level robustness. I'll kick these off and post artifacts.

samir: thanks — when you post the topk diff CSV i'll do a fast analysis for id flips and propose candidate mitigation (recalibration, small retrain with noise augmentation).

leo: also file a perf note for runtime nondet risk — we should ensure deterministic kernels for int4 in dedicated infra. opened infra ticket INF-1987 earlier.

ginny: noted. will pin the runs in the CI and add ticket refs. tagging @tara for followups on small-cluster examples. :thumbsup:

tara: got it — i'll label ~30 representative flips for error analysis and draft quick prompteval to see if semantic content actually changed vs retrieval noise.

ginny: thanks all — will update thread with sweep artifacts. plan to try per-channel int4 + noise-augmented fine-tune next if results hold. :rocket:
